Greene Part A Amendment No. 114 to H.R. 4016 would delete the whole printed section 8067 identified by the exact offered amendment. That section directs one $500 million allocation from amounts appropriated under Procurement, Defense-Wide and Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Defense-Wide, not $500 million from each account. It allocates $60 million for the Secretary of Defense to provide to the Government of Israel for Iron Dome procurement subject to the named procurement agreement; $127 million for the Short Range Ballistic Missile Defense program, including cruise-missile defense research and development; $40 million for SRBMD co-production in the United States and Israel; $100 million for the upper-tier component, all of that $100 million for Arrow 3 co-production in the United States and Israel; and $173 million for the Arrow System Improvement Program including development of a long-range ground and airborne detection suite. Within the targeted directive, the SRBMD and Arrow 3 co-production allocations are subject to their respective U.S.-Israeli co-production agreements and each nation's laws, regulations and procedures. These five amounts total $500 million; the upper-tier co-production amount is not a second additional $100 million. Deleting this allocation directive does not establish a $500 million reduction in the overall account totals, a ban on all assistance to Israel or repeal of the referenced agreements. It changes this particular direction for the use of amounts under the named accounts; the broader appropriation totals and other authorities are not rewritten by the deletion instruction. The retained complete own offering, resumed recorded question and report identify this exact child and the complete reported section 8067 is its target; parent final-passage meaning, geopolitical debate and another domain's conclusion are not used to supply its meaning. The House rejected this amendment on civil July 18, 2025 in the legislative July 17 Record,6–422, with 9 Not Voting. A Yea supports adopting this exact deletion; a Nay opposes that deletion without establishing a stance on the whole bill or all Israeli assistance. No actual outlay reduction, changed defense capability, program delivery, motive or enactment is inferred. Infrastructure/Technology membership remains an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal: removal of specified missile procurement and explicit research and development allocations is proposed under the existing direct technology/research-governance rule, with independent membership review required before acceptance.

Perry Amendment No. 26 to H.R. 4553 inserts a $13 million reduction after the $13 million amount on reported page 37, line 9, and a matching $13 million increase after the $0 Spending Reduction Account amount in section 512 on reported page 74, line 5. The complete targeted heading appropriates $13 million for DOE administrative expenses necessary in carrying out the Advanced Technology Vehicles Manufacturing Loan Program, available until September 30, 2027. The amendment would reduce this proposed administrative appropriation to zero and increase that bill's Spending Reduction Account from $0 to $13 million. The $13 million is administrative funding, not loan principal or credit subsidy; the amendment does not repeal the loan program or cancel existing loans. It does not transfer $13 million to a different grant program, establish a $13 million reduction in actual outlays or demonstrate any particular project, employment or vehicle-production result. The retained 2024 operative section 17013 supplies the program mechanism: conditional facility/engineering-integration awards and a distinct direct-loan program subject to appropriated funds, with applicant/repayment/labor and other statutory conditions. Its vehicle definition extends beyond passenger electric cars to specified light/medium/heavy vehicles, trains/locomotives, maritime vessels, aircraft and hyperloop technology. Those definitions and historical time limits are context, not new eligibility rules created by this amendment or a complete September 2025 consolidated-law certification. The separate July 2025 Public Law 119-21 section 50402 repeals IRA section 50142 and rescinds its unobligated balances; that narrower funding provision is not substituted for repeal of all section 17013 or proof of every surviving balance. This proposed administrative appropriation and the separate rescission are distinct. No present borrower entitlement, available balance, actual shutdown, enacted spending reduction or change to program eligibility is inferred. The complete own offering and resumed recorded choice identify this exact amendment; it was rejected 140–286 with 10 Not Voting on September 3, 2025. A Yea supports this paired administrative reduction/Spending Reduction Account increase; a Nay opposes that pair without establishing a stance on the whole bill, every vehicle technology or every program loan. Direct transportation/technology program-governance membership remains an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal requiring independent review, with no acceptance or publication authority.

Perry Amendment No. 28 to H.R. 4553 would reduce the reported Northern Border Regional Commission appropriation of $33,319,727 by $13,319,727, leaving $20 million, and increase the bill's section 512 Spending Reduction Account from $0 by $13,319,727. These are the two exact page/line instructions, not a separate new grant appropriation or an abolition of the Commission. The targeted appropriation is for Commission activities authorized by subtitle V of title 40 and remains available until expended. Its proviso allowing administrative expenses notwithstanding section 15751(b) remains unchanged; the amendment does not reinstate that section's ordinary 10-percent administrative cap or turn this appropriation into grants only. The retained statutory context permits grants for transportation, basic public and telecommunications infrastructure and also workforce/business development, distressed-area public services, conservation/recreation/open space, renewable energy, community economic-development capacity and other subtitle purposes. Section 15501 requires at least 40 percent of GRANT AMOUNTS for the combined transportation/basic/telecommunications/renewable-energy categories; that is not 40 percent of this entire appropriation, not transportation alone and not a project-specific allocation of the proposed reduction. Grants can combine other sources. Contribution limits depend on county distress, regional-project conditions and other qualifications; the retained Northern Border COVID-related cost-share waiver is not erased. The separate $40 million annual authorization for each Commission for fiscal years 2025–2029 is not this proposed appropriation and is not itself cash made available. This amendment does not rewrite those authorizing/grant rules, cancel other appropriations or balances, or establish which grants or administrative activities would receive less money. No particular infrastructure-project loss, borrower/grantee eligibility, actual outlay savings, current available balance or complete consolidated-law certification is inferred. The whole mixed-purpose Commission appropriation, rather than a selected desirable component, is the subject of this paired reduction. The House rejected it 124–303 with 9 Not Voting on September 3, 2025; initial voice ayes are not final adoption. A Yea supports adopting this exact pair; a Nay opposes it without establishing support for every Commission grant, the whole parent bill or any motive. Direct infrastructure/technology grant-governance membership remains an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal requiring independent review of the mixed-purpose boundary; no acceptance or publication authority is conferred.

Patronis Part A Amendment No. 9 to H.R. 3838 would delete paragraphs (4) and (10) of 10 U.S.C. 2911(e), renumber the remaining paragraphs as printed, and repeal the whole of section 2922g. In the retained 2024 operative subsection 2911(e), the deleted provisions require consideration of alternative-energy initiatives including alternative fuels and hybrid-electric military drives, and of the value of electric, hybrid-electric and high-efficiency fleet vehicles in developing and implementing Defense energy-performance goals and the master plan. The other thirteen listed considerations are not repealed by those deletions. The separate retained section 2922g has two distinct time regimes. Before October 1, 2035, it requires an electric/hybrid/plug-in-hybrid lease or procurement preference only when vehicles meet Defense needs and are commercially available at reasonably comparable cost including operation; tactical combat vehicles are excepted, and another fossil-fuel-reducing technology may receive a preference under the Secretary's stated energy-plan determination. Beginning October 1, 2035, the separate requirement covers defined nontactical vehicles under contracts entered, renewed, modified or amended on or after that date. Its alternatives are electric/zero-emission vehicles with industry-accepted interoperable/safe charging connections, advanced-biofuel-powered vehicles, or hydrogen-powered vehicles. This is not an immediate electric-only requirement for all military vehicles. The future requirement also has the printed case-by-case alternative-technology authorization conditioned on reduced fossil-fuel use, consistency with the energy plan and impracticability of the listed choices; the Secretary may waive the future requirement and may not delegate that waiver authority. Repealing the whole section removes its conditional preference, future requirement and related exceptions/authorizations/definitions as a unit; it does not create a new ban on electric or hybrid procurement, require the purchase of conventional-fuel vehicles, or eliminate all Defense energy-planning law. The advanced-biofuel category incorporates 7 U.S.C. 8101(3)(A); no expanded feedstock list or individual vehicle/fuel eligibility determination is supplied. The complete retained target provisions are qualified 2024 baselines, not a comprehensive September 2025 consolidated-law or implementing-contract review. No present purchase mix, actual emissions/cost/readiness effect, vendor entitlement, savings, enacted repeal or motive is inferred. The House agreed to this exact child 224–208 with 1 Present and 4 Not Voting on September 10, 2025. Present is a resolved nondirectional status and does not supply a Yea or Nay stance; aggregate totals do not assign that status to a particular member. A Yea supports adopting the paired planning deletions and whole-section repeal; a Nay opposes that whole choice without establishing a separate stance on each technology or the full NDAA. Direct transportation/technology procurement and planning membership remains an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal requiring independent review before acceptance or publication.

Greene, offering as Davidson's designee, Part A Amendment No. 20 to H.R. 3838 would prohibit obligation or expenditure of the described funds for research, development, procurement and promotion of cell cultured meat. The full funding clause names two descriptions: funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act, or funds otherwise made available for fiscal year 2026 for the Department of Defense. The first funding description is Act-authorized funds, not merely funds appropriated by this Act. The other description retains its fiscal year 2026 and Department of Defense qualifications. Neither description is replaced with an invented account list or a restriction only to the bill's own actual appropriations. Authorization and appropriation are distinct; the amendment does not itself appropriate or rescind a specified dollar amount. All four activities are part of this one choice: research, development, procurement and promotion, not only research or only procurement. Its funding-use restriction is not a general consumer product ban: the text does not establish a general prohibition on manufacture, sale, purchase or consumption using private funds outside the described funding restriction, decide food safety or nutritional quality, or impose a ban under every Federal agency, fiscal year or source of money. The term cell cultured meat is used as printed; no expanded product/feedstock list, FDA approval determination, current funding eligibility or comprehensive account/application map is supplied. No existing project, amount of spending, future research result, procurement loss, consumer outcome, motive or enacted policy is inferred. The direct restriction on research and development funding is retained together with procurement and promotion; a narrower component is not selected as the whole meaning. The complete own offering and the independently retained printed report clause agree on that funding/activities sentence. The House rejected this exact child 194–236, with 1 Present and 6 Not Voting on September 10, 2025; preliminary voice ayes do not override that rejection. Present is nondirectional, and aggregate chamber totals do not assign a status to a particular member. A Yea supports adopting this whole funding-use restriction; a Nay opposes that exact choice without establishing support for a specific product, private purchase, company, scientific claim or the full NDAA. Infrastructure/Technology membership remains an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal under the existing direct technology/research-governance criterion, with the broader food-procurement/promotion boundary requiring independent review before acceptance or publication.

H.R. 3109 would require the Secretary of Energy, not later than 90 days after enactment of its report section, to direct the National Petroleum Council to prepare and submit a report to the Secretary of Energy and Congress and to make that report publicly available. The 90-day deadline is for the Secretary to direct the Council, not an express 90-day deadline for completing the report. The complete report mandate covers the role and energy-security contributions of United States petrochemical refineries, including supply reliability of liquid fuels and feedstocks and fuel affordability; analyses and projections of existing capacity, expansion opportunities and risks; an assessment of Federal or State executive actions, regulations or policies that have caused or contributed to capacity decline; and recommendations for Federal agencies and Congress to encourage increased capacity. These are commissioned assessment and recommendation topics, not this platform's findings that any policy caused decline or that capacity, reliability or affordability will improve. The report must go to both named recipients and be made public; public availability does not by itself create a new data platform or mandate a particular publication technology. The choice does not itself permit, fund, construct or require expansion of any refinery, repeal a regulation, adopt a recommendation, appropriate a dollar amount or require a particular fuel mix or company. No existing report, particular project, spending, actual capacity decline, causal effect, future price, employment, environmental, reliability or geopolitical outcome is established. The complete retained House-engrossed body is the whole choice; no narrower favorable reporting component or parent energy agenda is substituted. A Yea supports passing this whole report-direction and publication requirement; a Nay opposes passing that exact requirement, without establishing a position on every refinery, fuel, regulation or recommendation. Not Voting is a resolved nondirectional observation and establishes neither support nor opposition, reason for absence, motive or character. Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal under the existing direct infrastructure-capacity planning/reporting criterion, pending independent review of the whole mandate and completeness before acceptance or publication.
